title: DataLake Architecture Overview
body:
DataLake Architecture Overview
Owner: Technology (Data Engineering)
Author: Michael Jones, Data Engineer
Last updated: 2026-07-28
Classification: Internal

Purpose
This document describes how the DataLake is structured, what feeds it, and which downstream systems rely on it. It is intended for engineers on call in Technology and for the Risk, Compliance, and Lending teams that own consumers of the lake. DataLake is classified as a standard-tier system, but several critical systems sit downstream of it, so treat incidents with that in mind.

Dependency Position
In the platform dependency graph DataLake has no upstream dependencies. It is a landing zone, and producers push into it. We deliberately avoid pull-based ingestion from other production services, so an outage in a source system never blocks the lake from starting or serving.

Downstream consumers are:
- FraudScore (Compliance): feature tables for real-time transaction scoring
- AMLMonitor (Compliance): transaction history and counterparty aggregates for alert generation
- CreditScoring (Lending): historical performance data for the decisioning models
- ReportingBI (Risk): management and regulatory dashboards

Because FraudScore and AMLMonitor are critical and depend on the lake, and PaymentsGateway depends on FraudScore, a prolonged DataLake stall can propagate to payments. The freshness monitors described below exist for that reason.

Layers
The lake is organized into three zones.

Raw zone: immutable, append-only copies of what producers send, partitioned by source and business date. Nothing in this zone is edited. If a producer sends bad data, we land a correction and let the curated layer reconcile it.

Curated zone: cleaned, conformed, and deduplicated tables with consistent keys for instruments, accounts, and legal entities. Schema changes here go through a review by Data Engineering plus the consuming team lead.

Serving zone: purpose-built marts for each consumer, for example the feature tables FraudScore reads and the reporting marts behind ReportingBI. Marts are rebuilt on a schedule and are safe to drop and regenerate from curated data.

Ingestion Sources
PricingSvc publishes end-of-day valuation snapshots and curve data to the raw zone as files. This is a push from PricingSvc, so the lake does not call it. Intraday ticks are not stored here; MarketDataFeed retains those, and only the closing set reaches us via PricingSvc.

Other feeds include general ledger extracts from GLCore, position snapshots from PositionStore, payment events from PaymentsGateway, and client reference data exports from ClientHub. Each feed has a named producer contact and an expected arrival window documented in the feed registry.

Access and Identity
Human access to query tooling and notebooks is authenticated through AuthSSO, with entitlements mapped to AD-style groups per team. Pipeline service accounts are managed separately inside the lake's own secrets store so that an AuthSSO disruption does not stop batch loads. Data Engineering reviews entitlements quarterly with Compliance.

Sensitive client attributes are tokenized at the curated layer. Analysts working in the serving zone see surrogate client keys, not names or contact details. Any request for re-identification goes through Compliance and is logged.

Scheduling and Freshness
Batch loads run overnight after the GLCore close. The target is for all curated tables to be refreshed by 05:30 Eastern, ahead of the morning Risk reporting run. Freshness monitors alert the Technology on-call in #it-ops when a table misses its window, and page if a table feeding FraudScore or AMLMonitor is more than two hours late.

Known Limitations
- Backfills of more than 90 days compete with nightly loads and should be scheduled on weekends.
- Lineage tracking is partial for older ReportingBI marts; we are migrating these to the standard build framework.
- ReconLegacy does not read from the lake and continues to use its own Oracle store.

Operational Runbook Pointers
For a late feed, first confirm with the producer team whether the file was sent, then check the raw zone landing log. For a failed curated build, rerun the single table before rerunning the whole DAG. For a consumer complaint about stale data, check the freshness dashboard before escalating.

Questions go to Michael Jones or the Data Engineering rotation in #it-ops.
